subject: Re: RFP: Dedicated GPU mix and reservation commitments for Silhouette Health
messages:
From: Dan Barnes <dbarnes@silhouettehealth.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Malhotra <priya.malhotra@silhouettehealth.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-14T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: RFP: Dedicated GPU mix and throughput clarifications

Laura / Redwood team,

Thanks for sending over the RFP intake and the template. We're compiling internal requirements and have a handful of clarifying questions so we can populate your capacity template correctly: 

1) Target SLAs: we plan to drive both chat-style long-context generation (avg 1k context, 1–3 tokens/sec per request) and high-throughput embedding/rerank workloads. For sizing, what 95/99 pctl latency SLOs do you assume per model class for Dedicated reservations?

2) GPU options: can you share recommended GPU families (A100-40/A100-80, H100) for a mixed workload? We are sensitive to per-token cost and want to balance throughput for embeddings vs tail latency for chat.

3) Commitment window: what are your standard reservation terms (12/24/36 months) and how do burst credits/overage work operationally?

4) Mapping: can you provide an example mapping of concurrent requests / sustained QPS -> reserved GPU count for the two workload profiles (chat gen, embeddings)? If you have a matrix we can drop into our procurement bundle, that'd be ideal.

5) Security/region constraint: our first deployment will be in us-west with private VPC; any regional GPU limits we should be aware of?

Please see attached: Silhouette_RFP_template.xlsx — we've started filling high-level traffic estimates. We'll need the capacity matrix back to finalize our procurement ask.

Appreciate a short response with the above answered; happy to set a quick call if it's easier.

Thanks,
Dan Barnes
Head of ML Platform
Silhouette Health
Attachments: Silhouette_RFP_template.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: RFP: Dedicated GPU mix and throughput clarifications

Dan — thanks, this is very clear. I've attached a tailored capacity matrix (SH_RFP_capacity_matrix.xlsx) and our GPU profile guide (redwood_gpu_profiles_v1.pdf). High level answers below; the attached matrix includes a few common traffic scenarios so your procurement team can plug numbers into the RFP.

Summary answers (short):
- Typical latency SLOs we design for: 95p <= 150ms (chat short-context), 95p <= 250ms (long-context generation, depending on model length); 99p targets are typically 1.5–3x the 95p depending on tail policies. For embeddings, 95p <= 70ms for per-batch pipelines. These are achievable with 1–2x the reserved GPU counts in the matrix if you enable prefix/KV caching.

- GPU mix recommendation (starter/baseline):
  * Latency-first (chat, 1k context, 4–8 concurrent): H100-80GB nodes for the inference pools that serve front-door generation.
  * Throughput-first (embeddings, batched): A100-80GB or A100-40GB with larger batch sizing and mixed-precision quantization.

- Example mapping (from attached matrix, excerpt):
  * Chat profile: 200 sustained QPS (avg 1k token responses) -> reserve 8 H100-80GB nodes; allows 99p within target under our default batching and 20% burst headroom.
  * Embedding profile: 4k QPS (256-token avg, batched) -> reserve 6 A100-80GB nodes; batching reduces effective per-token cost 2.5x relative to single-request path.

- Commitment windows: we support 12 / 24 / 36-month contracts. Longer terms unlock deeper unit pricing and larger guaranteed burst pools. Standard model: monthly committed baseline + 20% monthly burst credit pool; overages billed at published committed overage rates. We can model a custom burst pool if you need a seasonal cushion.

- Region constraints: us-west has H100 & A100 capacity today; for large 100+ GPU reservations we coordinate a lead time of 6–8 weeks to ensure allocation and validate networking/VPC placement.

Next steps we recommend: (1) review the attached capacity matrix and drop in your expected QPS columns; (2) confirm preferred commitment term (12/24/36 months) and any hard latency SLOs; (3) schedule a 30-min technical kickoff so Marcus can align kernel/quantization options with your models.

Attachments: SH_RFP_capacity_matrix.xlsx, redwood_gpu_profiles_v1.pdf

—
Laura Bennett

Subject: Re: RFP: Dedicated GPU mix and throughput clarifications

Adding a quick technical note on sizing assumptions so the numbers in Laura's matrix map to model-level throughput: 

- Baseline assumptions used in the matrix: medium-sized autoregressive generation model (context 1k tokens), token throughput measured as ~450 tokens/sec per H100-80GB under continuous batching and KV cache for prefix tokens. That yields ~0.45 tokens/ms; for a 1k-token response the modeled server-side decode takes ~2.2s (amortized across concurrent requests).

- Embeddings: we assume batched throughput of ~1.8M tokens/sec per A100-80GB with int8 quantization / fused kernels when using batch sizes 64–256. If your embedding model uses smaller dimensions we can map these numbers down proportionally in the matrix.

- Quantization / kernel fit: recommended path for mixed workload is to keep the chat pool on float16 H100s (minimal quantization to preserve quality), and run heavy embedding/transformer-batched work on quantized A100 pools. We can support q4_0/ptq for embeddings and still hit your cost targets while preserving 99p quality checks.

- Autoscaling / burst behavior: our Dedicated offering allows a configured burst window up to +30% of baseline with pre-agreed lead time. For sub-minute scale spikes (e.g. flash traffic) we suggest a small front-door warm pool of pre-warmed H100s to avoid cold-start tails.

I've uploaded an internal runbook excerpt referenced by the matrix — see the Drive link Laura shared. Happy to walk through specific model configs on the call.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal Applied ML Engineer — Redwood Inference

- We're inclined toward a 36-month commitment for the baseline pools (prioritizing H100s for chat, A100s for embeddings). Please prepare a model-level commitment worksheet (monthly GPU counts by node type) we can attach to our Master Services Agreement.

- Legal asked for a signed MSA stub to attach to the internal purchase requisition — I've attached a blank MA stub request. If you can provide a countersigned placeholder (ma_stub_signed.pdf) we can progress approvals in parallel to the tech kickoff.

- Let's set a 30-minute technical kickoff next week (Priya / Dan / infra / Redwood engineering) to go through the matrix rows that correspond to our peak seasonal scenario. Our calendar has availability Tues/Wed afternoons PST.

Please confirm who will be on the kickoff and attach the commitment worksheet when you reply.
